bluf: Acadia is a US founder led retail media agency, founded 2021 by Jared Belsky (CEO) and Sean Belnick, selling full service retail media on Amazon, Walmart and Instacart with analytics and media mix modeling behind it. The record leads with awards: the homepage bills it as Ad Age Media Agency of the Year 2026 after a 2024 Ad Age and MediaPost double. With no AI posture, pricing model, case study text, news or jobs on record, where it is going is unstated. A rival should know that its client book is three names with no described work, and its own house contradicts three of the four lines the Radar tested.
doing:
The positioning line reads as a full service growth agency led by retail media and marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart, Instacart), with paid media, analytics and MMM, SEO, CRO and social behind it: it sells the marketplace ad budget first and the surrounding media and measurement second. The headline claim is an award: the homepage title and meta bill it as Ad Age Media Agency of the Year 2026, after a 2024 double of Ad Age Performance Agency of the Year and MediaPost Independent Agency of the Year; the about page says no other agency has won both in the same year. Claims quoted as claims.

The services page lists Full Service Retail Media, Analytics & Business Intelligence, Media Mix Modeling, Paid Media, Programmatic, CRO, Performance Creative, Influencer Marketing, Organic Social, SEO, Retention Marketing and Multi-Location. Two lead capabilities score 3: Data & Measurement (Analytics & BI, Media Mix Modeling and incrementality testing) and Retail Media (Full Service Retail Media leads the homepage, with Amazon, Walmart, Instacart, Target, Kroger, Chewy and Ulta pages). Core lines at score 2 are Creator & Influencer (a performance driven influencer team), Local (the Multi-Location service and store visit case stories for European Wax Center, 1,100 locations, and Fresh Thyme), Paid Search and Paid Social (the Paid Media page names search, social and media agency of record work, buying TikTok and Meta) and SEO. No proprietary products and no partners are listed.

AI posture: none in the record; AI Search / GEO and AI Automation both score 0. Moves in date order: founded 2021 by ex 360i CEO Jared Belsky and Bizchair founder Sean Belnick; the 2024 award double; the 2026 Ad Age title. Pricing signals: none. Conspicuously absent for a retail media agency: case study text, news, jobs, partner badges, any AI statement, and Web & Product at 0.
clients:
The record describes a mid-market client type, with verticals listed as Beauty, Pets, Restaurants, Apparel, CPG, Health & Wellness and B2B, and a US home market with no offices listed. The client book on record is three names, all carried as case study evidence on the homepage: TRUBAR, Fresh Thyme and European Wax Center. None of the three carries a case study title, a URL slug or a press line describing the work, so all three sit in the needs read as engagement named only (N0), and the need is inferred from what Acadia leads with.

Inferred needs, said as such: European Wax Center appears in the Local capability note as a store visit case story across 1,100 locations, so the likely need is local and lead generation for a multi location brand; Fresh Thyme appears in the same store visit note, so the same local demand read applies; TRUBAR has no note beyond the name, and given the sold mix the inferred need is commerce and marketplaces, the retail media line Acadia leads with. The record shows no shared clients: none of the three appears on another tracked agency's book, and the shared count is 0.

The book is entirely names only, 3 of 3, which the openings read flags as thin evidence of what the agency does for them. What the base needs next, as a judgment: the Horus read places Acadia best for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), both driven by its Data & Measurement line, so a client base of CPG and beauty brands buying marketplace media is likely to need measurement and incrementality work more than hours of campaign management, with moderate confidence given that no client evidence describes any engagement.
house: Say and do: the Radar tested four lines against Acadia's own house and found 1 of 4 practised. Paid Search is contradicted: it sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own in the Transparency Center (count 0). LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: no LinkedIn ads of its own; the library note says 258 ads match the name query across all advertisers, the first page shows 24 cards, and near name advertisers Acadia Pharmaceuticals (7) and Acadia Healthcare (3) were excluded. Creator & Influencer is contradicted: no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube channel is linked from its site, only LinkedIn and Facebook. Paid Social is corroborated by a linkedin_insight pixel. Publishing cadence was not measured: sitemap count 0, 0 URLs in 90 and 365 days, velocity unmeasured rather than idle. Tags are gtm, linkedin_insight and hubspot on WordPress; no test tools, ABM stack or llms.txt, no AI crawlers blocked, AI URL count 0, Meta and TikTok status not recorded.
market:
The Horus read scores Acadia 7.9 on the tailwind index, 39th percentile, band Neutral, sold mix at 17:23 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum), resilience 34.3. Best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), carried by Data & Measurement; most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), driven by Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV. Best fit: The Walled Oasis at 50/100. Making P2 and P4; partial on P3 and P7; absent on P1, P6 and P8; P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read: 51.1, band Breeze, 32nd percentile, migration 48.6 against displacement 53.6. The verdict says 49 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (9) and Local (8) carrying the most movable hours; the shore would be 65% South and Southeast Asia and 25% Latin America; the footprint is inferred, with no hub offices or onshore claims listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the say and do gap: Acadia sells paid search with no Google ads of its own in the Transparency Center, paid social with no LinkedIn ads, and influencer work with no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube channel on its site. A rival whose own house is in order can very likely lead with that contradiction (moderate confidence). Falsifier: Acadia's own ads in either library, or a linked creator channel, at the next compile.

The book is contestable because it is unevidenced, 3 of 3 clients names only: European Wax Center, Fresh Thyme and TRUBAR are questions to ask, not stories to counter; a multi location offer built on LSAs and Sponsored Places, where Acadia is only partial, is likely to get a hearing with a 1,100 location brand. No public pricing model is recorded: an outcome priced retail media offer is a conversation it cannot have in public (likely, low confidence). With no ads tested inside AI assistants and no AI posture, a rival showing assistant ad results or an audited AI visibility number likely sets the price against it; its KJ6 exposure rests on the Paid Search and Paid Social hours an output priced rival undercuts.
watch: Indicator I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, next reading December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV would strengthen KJ4, the judgment Acadia is best placed for, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

Indicator I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, next reading 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas bear on KJ8 and on the creator line Acadia sells without a linked channel.

The 2026 Ad Age Media Agency of the Year claim on the homepage is the dated move to follow up: whether it is carried beyond the title tag into case studies or news would change the thin evidence read.
The next Radar compile after 2026-09-28 refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; a sitemap count above 0 or a Google ads record would rewrite the house section.
